# twnty

> twnty is a free, open-source (MIT) desktop app for macOS and Windows that reminds you to follow the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds. A pair of friendly eyes lives in your menu bar or system tray and slowly turns bloodshot red as 20 minutes pass; when time is up, a gentle break reminder appears with a 20-second countdown. No accounts, no telemetry, everything stays on your computer.

twnty is for anyone who works at a screen for long stretches (developers, designers, writers, students) and wants a low-friction way to build the habit of resting their eyes. It costs nothing. It runs on macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel, universal build) and Windows (x64).

## Features

- Five selectable eye styles: Classic, Googly, Cat, Sparkle, Dot
- macOS menu bar icon and Windows system tray icon with 10 progressive redness stages, plus an optional live countdown on macOS
- Optional floating desktop companion: transparent, always-on-top, draggable eyes that blink, follow the cursor, and smile after a break
- Break reminder as a centered card or a full-screen calm color field, with a 20-second countdown and a soft singing-bowl chime
- Pauses after 5 minutes without input; defers popups during full-screen apps; opens on the monitor your cursor is on; optional strict mode hides Skip
- Daily stats (breaks taken vs. skipped) and configurable work/rest intervals

## Privacy

- No accounts, no telemetry, no analytics in the app
- All settings and stats are stored locally on your device

## FAQ

### Is twnty free?
Yes. It is free and open source under the MIT license.

### Which platforms does it support?
macOS (universal: Apple Silicon and Intel) and Windows.

### What is the 20-20-20 rule?
Every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet (about 6 meters) away for 20 seconds, to give your eyes a rest from close-up screen focus.

### Does twnty collect my data?
No. There are no accounts and no telemetry; everything stays local.

### Why does my OS warn me when installing?
Current builds are unsigned. On macOS, right-click the app and choose Open (or use System Settings, Privacy & Security, Open Anyway). On Windows SmartScreen, choose More info, then Run anyway.
